items.followUp: Differentiate between primary memory and secondary storage.

rubric.why: Shows that storage keeps data for long-term use.
rubric.description: Identifies storage as long-term or permanent data retention.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that storage retains data long-term or permanently, or identifying it as secondary storage.

rubric.why: Shows a key distinction of computer memory.
rubric.description: Identifies memory as temporary/volatile or directly accessible by the CPU.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that memory is temporary or volatile, or that the CPU directly accesses it.

modelAnswer: Storage keeps data and programs for long-term use, usually on secondary devices such as a hard drive.
Memory holds data and instructions currently needed by the CPU; it is generally temporary and faster to access.
Therefore, storage is for long-term retention, while memory is used for current processing.
Example: a hard drive is storage; RAM is memory.
Similar practice: State two differences between RAM and a hard drive.

items.followUp: Draw the truth table for the compound proposition p OR q.

rubric.why: The truth table must include every possible combination of p and q.
rubric.description: Shows all four possible input combinations for p and q.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including the four input pairs TT, TF, FT and FF.

rubric.why: For conjunction, p AND q is true only when both p and q are true.
rubric.description: Gives the correct output for p AND q for all four input combinations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct output column: T, F, F, F.

modelAnswer: For the compound proposition p AND q, the truth table is:
p, q, p AND q
T, T, T
T, F, F
F, T, F
F, F, F
Similar practice: Draw the truth table for p OR q.

items.followUp: What is meant by the Internet?

rubric.why: This states the defining structure of the Internet.
rubric.description: Defines the Internet as an interconnection or network of networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the Internet as interconnected networks or a network of networks.

rubric.why: Adds the global scope or communication purpose of the Internet.
rubric.description: Mentions that the connected networks operate globally or enable communication.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the networks are connected worldwide or enable devices/users to communicate.

modelAnswer: The Internet is a worldwide network of interconnected computer networks, so it is called a network of networks.
These networks communicate and exchange information using common protocols such as TCP/IP.
Similar practice: Define a computer network and give one example.

items.followUp: Define a multipoint connection and give an example.

rubric.why: A point-to-point connection links exactly two endpoints.
rubric.description: States that the connection is directly between two devices or nodes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the two endpoints.

rubric.why: A point-to-point link is a dedicated/direct link; an example is required by the question.
rubric.description: Describes a direct or dedicated link and gives a suitable example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a direct/dedicated link or a suitable example such as a direct cable or telephone line.

modelAnswer: A point-to-point connection is a direct link between two devices, with the link used by those two endpoints.
Example: two computers connected directly by a cable.
Similar practice: Describe a multipoint connection and give an example.

items.followUp: How many bits are used in an IPv4 address? Give an example.

rubric.why: IPv4 uses a 32-bit address divided into four octets.
rubric.description: States the length or four-part structure of an IPv4 address.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that IPv4 is 32 bits long or has four octets.

rubric.why: A valid example demonstrates the dotted-decimal form.
rubric.description: Gives an IPv4 example in dotted-decimal notation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid four-part dotted-decimal example.

modelAnswer: IPv4 (Internet Protocol version 4) is an addressing system that uses 32-bit addresses.
An IPv4 address is written as four decimal numbers separated by dots; for example, 192.168.1.1.
Similar practice: Define IPv6 and state the length of its addresses.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of a URL? Give one example.

rubric.why: URL is the abbreviation for Uniform Resource Locator.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing “Uniform Resource Locator.”

rubric.why: A URL locates a resource on the web; an example can demonstrate this.
rubric.description: Explains that a URL is a web resource's address or gives a valid URL example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a web/resource address or providing a valid URL.

modelAnswer: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator.
It is the address used to locate a resource on the Internet, for example, https://www.example.com.
Similar practice: Expand HTTP and state what it is used for.
